claims: Snell law gives n_water sin(θ_water) = n_air sin(θ_air). A ray from axial depth d reaches the surface at x = d tan(θ_water). Its backward extension has apparent depth x/tan(θ_air). At small angles, apparent/real depth approaches n_air/n_water, approximately three quarters.

Symmetric rays meet at an axial virtual point; wider bundles are not perfectly stigmatic. Four-to-about-three is the near-normal limit. The displayed twelve-degree water rays use exact refraction and a ratio slightly below three quarters.
limitations: Numerical checks complement the stated derivation; idealizations are explicit.
